old: but my father thought I needed exposure to customs beyond our own country.
new: but my father thought that, to complete my education, I needed to get to know customs other than those of my own country.
reason: Source: 'thought it necessary for the completion of my education' — the purpose clause was dropped.

old: an omen of the misery to come.
new: an omen, as it were, of the misery to come.
reason: Source hedge 'an omen, as it were' dropped (hedges are to be preserved).

old: But the consequences were fatal for her rescuer.
new: But the consequences of this rashness were fatal for her rescuer.
reason: Source: 'the consequences of this imprudence were fatal to her preserver' — the judgment 'imprudence' was dropped.

old: learn to count ourselves fortunate that at least some of our loved ones had been spared.
new: learn to count ourselves fortunate as long as even one of us remained whom death, the great plunderer, had not seized.
reason: Source: 'fortunate whilst one remains whom the spoiler has not seized' — the personified 'spoiler' (death) and the 'as long as one remains' condition were lost.

old: It felt wrong to leave
new: It felt like sacrilege to leave
reason: Source: 'It appeared to me sacrilege' — 'felt wrong' weakens a deliberate strong word (echoing 'sacrilege' in the previous paragraph).

old: when she gathered up the sunshine of her smiles
new: when she called back the sunshine of her smiles
reason: Source: 'she recalled the sunshine of her smiles' = brought them back after grief; 'gathered up' loses the sense of return.

old: Henry felt the injustice of being denied
new: Henry felt the misfortune of being denied
reason: Source: 'deeply felt the misfortune of being debarred' — 'injustice' imports a judgment the source does not make.

old: had longed to enter the wider world.
new: had longed to enter the world and take my place among other people.
reason: Source: 'longed to enter the world and take my station among other human beings' — second half dropped.

old: was taken to my room
new: was taken to my solitary lodgings
reason: Source: 'conducted to my solitary apartment' — 'solitary' continues the loneliness theme of the preceding paragraph.

old: Chance — or rather the evil influence that had claimed power over me from the moment I left my father's door —
new: Chance — or rather the evil influence, the Angel of Destruction, which took all-powerful control of me from the moment I turned my reluctant steps away from my father's door —
reason: Source names 'the Angel of Destruction, which asserted omnipotent sway over me from the moment I turned my reluctant steps' — the personification, 'omnipotent' and 'reluctant' were dropped.

old: I answered carelessly and mentioned
new: I answered carelessly and, partly out of contempt, mentioned
reason: Source: 'I replied carelessly, and partly in contempt, mentioned' — 'partly in contempt' dropped.

old: I went home not disappointed — I'd long considered those authors useless, as the professor said.
new: I went home not disappointed, for as I've said, I had long considered the authors the professor condemned to be useless.
reason: Source: 'for I have said that I had long considered those authors useless whom the professor reprobated' — 'as the professor said' drops the narrator's back-reference and blurs who judged them.

old: Looking back with perhaps too much philosophical clarity, I'd already drawn my own conclusions about science in my early years.
new: Perhaps I have described too philosophically and too neatly the conclusions I had come to about these studies in my early years.
reason: Source: 'In rather a too philosophical and connected a strain, perhaps, I have given an account of the conclusions...' — a narrator's comment on his own earlier account, which the candidate turns into a different claim.

old: whose hands seem made only for test tubes and microscopes,
new: whose hands seem made only to dabble in dirt, and their eyes only to pore over the microscope or the crucible,
reason: Source: 'whose hands seem only made to dabble in dirt, and their eyes to pore over the microscope or crucible' — the deliberately humble 'dabble in dirt' image and 'crucible' were replaced with 'test tubes'.

old: wrestling with something tangible.
new: wrestling with an enemy I could touch.
reason: Source: 'grappling with a palpable enemy' — 'enemy' dropped.

old: I spoke carefully, with the modesty a young student owes his teacher, without revealing the enthusiasm that was already driving my intended work.
new: I spoke carefully, with the modesty a young student owes his teacher, and let none of the enthusiasm driving my intended work slip out — my inexperience of life would have made me ashamed to.
reason: Source parenthesis '(inexperience in life would have made me ashamed)' giving the reason for concealment was dropped.

old: When I'd learned as much theory and practice as any professor at Ingolstadt could teach me, I thought about going home — until an incident extended my stay.
new: When I'd learned as much of the theory and practice of natural philosophy as any professor at Ingolstadt could teach me, staying there no longer helped my progress, so I thought of returning to my friends and my hometown — until an incident extended my stay.
reason: Source: 'my residence there being no longer conducive to my improvements, I thought of returning to my friends and my native town' — the reason and destination were dropped.

old: I succeeded in discovering the cause of life.
new: I succeeded in discovering the cause of generation and life.
reason: Source: 'the cause of generation and life' — 'generation' dropped.

old: I was like the man in the old tale who was buried alive with the dead and found a passage to life, aided only by one faint, flickering light.
new: I was like the Arabian in the Arabian Nights tale who was buried alive with the dead and found a passage back to life, aided only by one glimmering light that seemed useless.
reason: Source: 'like the Arabian who had been buried with the dead ... one glimmering and seemingly ineffectual light' — 'Arabian' (Sinbad, Arabian Nights) and 'seemingly ineffectual' were dropped.

old: how dangerous the pursuit of knowledge can be, and how much happier is the man who believes his small town is the whole world
new: how dangerous it is to acquire knowledge, and how much happier is the man who believes his hometown is the whole world
reason: Source: 'how dangerous is the acquirement of knowledge ... who believes his native town to be the world' — 'can be' softens the claim and 'small' replaces 'native'.

old: I might eventually — though it seemed impossible now — learn to restore life where death had claimed it.
new: I might in time — though I now found it impossible — restore life where death had apparently given the body over to decay.
reason: Source: '(although I now found it impossible) renew life where death had apparently devoted the body to corruption' — certainty softened to 'seemed' and the hedge 'apparently' dropped.

old: The one secret I possessed was the hope I'd dedicated myself to.
new: The hope I had dedicated myself to was a secret that I alone possessed.
reason: Source: 'One secret which I alone possessed' — 'I alone' dropped; also clearer aloud.

old: It was only a passing frenzy that made me feel the horror all the more sharply
new: It was only a passing trance, and it made me feel all the more sharply
reason: Source: 'a passing trance, that only made me feel with renewed acuteness' — 'the horror' is added interpretation and 'trance' became 'frenzy'.

old: I wanted to push aside everything related to my emotions until
new: I wanted, so to speak, to put off everything to do with my affections until
reason: Source: 'I wished, as it were, to procrastinate all that related to my feelings of affection' — hedge dropped and 'feelings of affection' broadened to 'emotions'.

old: I later thought my father would be unfair
new: At the time I thought my father would be unfair
reason: Source: 'I then thought' (at that time) — 'later' reverses the time frame against 'but I am now convinced'.

old: A person should always maintain
new: A perfect human being should always maintain
reason: Source: 'A human being in perfection ought always' — the ideal qualifier was dropped, making it a general command.

old: destroy your taste for simple pleasures,
new: destroy your taste for those simple pleasures that nothing can taint,
reason: Source: 'simple pleasures in which no alloy can possibly mix' — qualifier dropped.

old: I seemed more like a slave condemned to toil in a mine than an artist at his beloved work.
new: I seemed more like a slave condemned to toil in the mines, or in some other unhealthy trade, than an artist at his beloved work.
reason: Source: 'toil in the mines, or any other unwholesome trade' — second term dropped.

old: I realized I was holding the corpse
new: I thought I was holding the corpse
reason: Source: 'I thought that I held the corpse' — in a dream; 'realized' raises certainty.

old: the approach of the monstrous corpse
new: the approach of the demonic corpse
reason: Source: 'the demoniacal corpse' — narrator's demonic characterization flattened to 'monstrous'.

old: he became something not even Dante could have imagined.
new: it became a thing such as not even Dante could have imagined.
reason: Source switches deliberately from 'him' to 'it became a thing' at the moment of animation; the candidate keeps 'he'.

old: all necessary knowledge isn't found in bookkeeping.
new: all necessary knowledge isn't contained in the noble art of bookkeeping.
reason: Source: 'the noble art of book-keeping' — Clerval's irony dropped.

old: But nothing was there. The apartment was empty.
new: But nothing was there. I stepped fearfully inside. The apartment was empty.
reason: Source: 'I stepped fearfully in' dropped.

old: My loud, uncontrolled, frantic laughter
new: My loud, uncontrolled, heartless laughter
reason: Source: 'heartless laughter' — 'frantic' changes the quality described.

old: had turned suddenly to bewilderment.
new: had so strangely turned to bitterness.
reason: Source: 'so strangely turned to bitterness' — both the manner and the resulting emotion are changed.

old: had its origin in some terrible event.
new: had its origin in some strange and terrible event.
reason: Source: 'some uncommon and terrible event' — 'uncommon' dropped.

old: with frequent relapses that alarmed my friend,
new: with frequent relapses that alarmed and grieved my friend,
reason: Source: 'relapses that alarmed and grieved my friend' — 'grieved' dropped.

old: Could he be referring to the subject I didn't dare even think about?
new: Could he be hinting at a being I didn't dare even think about?
reason: Source: 'an object on whom I dared not even think' — 'on whom' marks a person (the creature); 'subject' loses that.

old: through a strange cruelty,
new: through some strange perversity,
reason: Source: 'through a strange perversity' — 'cruelty' changes the nature of the fault.

old: The democratic institutions of our country
new: The republican institutions of our country
reason: Source: 'The republican institutions' — Geneva was a republic; 'democratic' is a different claim.

old: for the same reason Ariosto gives for Angelica's beauty
new: for the same reason the Italian poet Ariosto gives for the beauty of his heroine Angelica
reason: Brief accurate gloss for an unfamiliar allusion when heard aloud (Angelica, heroine of Ariosto's Orlando Furioso).

old: Her mother, left with only her neglected daughter, was now childless except for her.
new: Apart from the daughter she had neglected, her mother was left childless.
reason: Source: 'with the exception of her neglected daughter, was left childless' — candidate sentence is redundant and confusing aloud.

old: This constant emotional abuse eventually threw Madame Moritz into a decline that at first increased her bitterness but ended with her death at the start of this past winter.
new: Her constant fretting eventually threw Madame Moritz into a decline, which at first made her even more irritable. But she is now at peace forever. She died when the cold weather first came, at the start of this past winter.
reason: Source: 'Perpetual fretting at length threw Madame Moritz into a decline, which at first increased her irritability, but she is now at peace for ever' — 'emotional abuse' invents a cause and misstates whose behavior caused the decline; 'at peace for ever' dropped.

old: He already has one or two little sweethearts,
new: He already has one or two little _wives_,
reason: Source italicizes '_wives_' as a playful joke; 'sweethearts' loses it (candidate keeps _italics_ elsewhere).

old: Her plain sister, Manon,
new: Her ugly sister, Manon,
reason: Source: 'Her ugly sister' — softened; do not soften period language.

old: Merely seeing a chemical instrument would bring back all the agony of my nervous breakdown.
new: Even when I was otherwise fully recovered, merely seeing a chemical instrument would bring back all the agony of my nervous symptoms.
reason: Source: 'When I was otherwise quite restored to health, the sight ... would renew all the agony of my nervous symptoms' — condition dropped; 'breakdown' changes 'symptoms'.

old: steered the conversation away by pleading complete ignorance of the subject.
new: steered the conversation away by pleading complete ignorance of the subject, and the talk turned to more general matters.
reason: Source: 'and the conversation took a more general turn' dropped.

old: noticing my expression of discomfort,
new: noticing the suffering in my face,
reason: Source: 'observing my face expressive of suffering' — 'discomfort' understates it.

old: How different from the bold, heroic poetry of Greece and Rome!
new: How different from the manly, heroic poetry of Greece and Rome!
reason: Source: 'the manly and heroical poetry' — period contrast softened to 'bold'.

old: Henry rejoiced in my cheerfulness and shared my feelings wholeheartedly.
new: Henry rejoiced in my cheerfulness and shared my feelings wholeheartedly. He did everything he could to amuse me, while also expressing the feelings that filled his own soul.
reason: Source: 'he exerted himself to amuse me, while he expressed the sensations that filled his soul' — whole clause dropped.

old: I strode along
new: I bounded along
reason: Source: 'I bounded along' — 'strode' loses the exuberance, and this sets up the fall in the next chapter.

old: blames herself as the cause of his death.
new: blames herself, unjustly, as the cause of his death.
reason: Source: 'accuses herself unjustly' — the father's judgment 'unjustly' was dropped.

old: the snowy mountains — the palaces of nature — were unchanged.
new: the snowy mountains — "the palaces of nature" — were unchanged.
reason: Source marks 'the palaces of nature' as a quotation (Byron); removing the quotation marks makes it Victor's own phrase.

old: Echoes bounced from Mount Saleve,
new: Echoes bounced from Mont Salêve,
reason: Source: 'Salêve' (and 'Mont Salêve' in 11,28) — diacritic stripped; AGENTS requires proper-noun accents to be preserved.

old: over the lake between Belrive and Copet.
new: over the part of the lake between the headland of Belrive and the village of Copêt.
reason: Source: 'between the promontory of Belrive and the village of Copêt' — accent stripped and place descriptors dropped.

old: the Mole, a peaked mountain
new: the Môle, a peaked mountain
reason: Source: 'the Môle' — accent stripped; 'the Mole' also reads aloud like the animal.

old: I considered chasing the monster, but it would have been hopeless. Another flash revealed him clinging to the rocks of the nearly vertical face of Mount Saleve.
new: I considered chasing the devil, but it would have been hopeless. Another flash revealed him clinging to the rocks of the nearly vertical face of Mont Salêve, a hill that borders Plainpalais to the south.
reason: Source: 'I thought of pursuing the devil' — epithet changed to 'monster'; also accent stripped and 'a hill that bounds Plainpalais on the south' dropped.

old: Nearly two years had passed since the night I first gave it life. Was this its first crime?
new: Nearly two years had passed since the night he first received life. Was this his first crime?
reason: Source: 'since the night on which he first received life; and was this his first crime?' — actor shifted to Victor and pronoun changed.

old: whose joy was in destruction and misery.
new: whose joy was in slaughter and misery.
reason: Source: 'whose delight was in carnage' — 'destruction' is weaker and vaguer.

old: endowed with the will and power to carry out purposes of horror.
new: endowed with the will and power to carry out horrors like the deed he had just committed.
reason: Source: 'purposes of horror, such as the deed which he had now done' — example clause dropped.

old: had met me at midnight on the slopes of an inaccessible mountain.
new: had met me at midnight among the cliffs of an inaccessible mountain.
reason: Source: 'among the precipices of an inaccessible mountain' — 'slopes' weakens the improbability Victor stresses.

old: the creature's strange nature would let it escape any pursuit,
new: the strange nature of the animal would let it escape any pursuit,
reason: Source: 'the strange nature of the animal' — narrator's epithet neutralized to 'creature'.

old: the sheer face of Mount Saleve?
new: the overhanging sides of Mont Salêve?
reason: Source: 'the overhanging sides of Mont Salêve' — accent stripped, 'Mont' changed.

old: Beloved parent! He still remained to me.
new: Beloved and revered parent! He still remained to me.
reason: Source: 'Beloved and venerable parent!' — 'venerable' dropped.

old: Its astounding horror would be dismissed as madness by everyone. Did anyone besides me — the creator — even believe in the existence of the living monument to arrogance and reckless ignorance that I had let loose on the world?
new: Its astounding horror would be dismissed as madness by ordinary people. Apart from me, its creator, did anyone exist who would believe — unless they saw it with their own eyes — in the living monument to arrogance and reckless ignorance that I had let loose on the world?
reason: Source: 'looked upon as madness by the vulgar. Did any one indeed exist, except I, the creator, who would believe, unless his senses convinced him, in the existence...' — 'by everyone' overstates, and the 'would believe unless his senses convinced him' condition was lost.

old: with every possible aggravation of injustice making her death memorable in its horror.
new: with every added disgrace that could make a murder memorable in its horror.
reason: Source: 'with every aggravation of infamy that could make the murder memorable in horror' — 'injustice' replaces 'infamy' (disgrace); simpler aloud.

old: Such a declaration would be dismissed as madness and wouldn't save Justine.
new: Such a declaration would be dismissed as the ravings of a madman and wouldn't clear Justine, who was suffering because of me.
reason: Source: 'would not have exculpated her who suffered through me' — Victor's self-accusation dropped.

old: She was composed, though clearly forcing herself to appear courageous. Her earlier confusion had already been cited as proof of guilt, so she steeled her mind to show courage.
new: She was composed, though her composure was clearly forced. Her earlier confusion had already been cited as proof of guilt, so she steeled her mind to show courage.
reason: Source: 'her tranquillity was evidently constrained' — the candidate states the courage point twice in succession.

old: The facts that emerged were damning — enough
new: Several strange facts combined against her — enough
reason: Source: 'Several strange facts combined against her' — 'strange' matters (they puzzle rather than simply damn).

old: an aunt in Chene,
new: an aunt in Chêne,
reason: Source: 'Chêne' — diacritic stripped.

old: But fear and hatred of the crime made them timid
new: But fear and hatred of the crime they supposed her guilty of made them timid
reason: Source: 'the crime of which they supposed her guilty' — the 'supposed' hedge dropped.

old: also have framed an innocent person for death?
new: also, in his hellish sport, have betrayed an innocent person to death and disgrace?
reason: Source: 'also in his hellish sport have betrayed the innocent to death and ignominy?' — 'hellish sport' and 'ignominy' dropped.

old: had already condemned the poor girl,
new: had already condemned my unhappy victim,
reason: Source: 'condemned my unhappy victim' — Victor's self-accusing term for Justine was neutralized.

old: failed to move the judges from their conviction.
new: failed to move the judges from their settled belief that this saintly sufferer was guilty.
reason: Source: 'from their settled conviction in the criminality of the saintly sufferer' — 'saintly sufferer' dropped.

old: All I would accomplish was declaring myself a madman without saving Justine.
new: I could have proclaimed myself a madman, but I could not have undone the sentence passed on my wretched victim.
reason: Source: 'Thus I might proclaim myself a madman, but not revoke the sentence passed upon my wretched victim' — 'my wretched victim' dropped.

old: all were the work of my cursed hands!
new: all were the work of my thrice-cursed hands!
reason: Source: 'thrice-accursed hands' — intensifier dropped.

old: He hopes only that if enough tears fall, inexorable fate may be satisfied and that destruction may stop before the peace of the grave finally succeeds your sad torment.
new: He would be happy beyond his hopes if this could satisfy inexorable fate, and if destruction would pause before the peace of the grave replaces your sad torment!
reason: Source: 'happy beyond his hopes, if thus inexorable fate be satisfied, and if the destruction pause...' — candidate reframes as a modest hope and invents 'if enough tears fall'.

old: He tried to inspire me with courage, drawing on his own clear conscience and blameless life.
new: Drawing on the feelings of his own clear conscience and blameless life, he tried to give me strength and to awaken the courage to drive away the dark cloud hanging over me.
reason: Source: 'to inspire me with fortitude and awaken in me the courage to dispel the dark cloud which brooded over me' — second purpose dropped.

old: but isn't it our duty to the survivors to control our grief? Excessive sorrow
new: but isn't it our duty to the survivors not to add to their unhappiness by a show of excessive grief? It's also a duty you owe yourself, for excessive sorrow
reason: Source: 'refrain from augmenting their unhappiness by an appearance of immoderate grief? It is also a duty owed to yourself' — the reason and the whole 'duty owed to yourself' sentence were dropped.

old: Geneva's gates shut regularly at ten, and being confined within the city walls had become unbearable.
new: Geneva's gates shut regularly at ten, and it was impossible to stay out on the lake after that hour, so living within the city walls had become unbearable to me.
reason: Source: 'and the impossibility of remaining on the lake after that hour' — dropped, though it explains the boating that follows.

old: I thought of Elizabeth, whom I loved dearly
new: I thought of Elizabeth, so heroic and so full of suffering, whom I loved dearly
reason: Source: 'the heroic and suffering Elizabeth' — epithets dropped.

old: leave them unprotected against the monster I'd let loose among them?
new: leave them exposed and unprotected against the malice of the fiend I'd let loose among them?
reason: Source: 'exposed and unprotected to the malice of the fiend' — 'fiend' changed to 'monster', and 'malice' dropped.

old: My hatred of this creature was beyond description.
new: My hatred of this fiend was beyond description.
reason: Source: 'My abhorrence of this fiend' — epithet neutralized to 'creature'.

old: She no longer took pleasure in anything.
new: She no longer took pleasure in her usual occupations.
reason: Source: 'no longer took delight in her ordinary occupations' — broadened to 'anything'.

old: The first sorrow sent to teach us that earth is not heaven had reached her,
new: The first of those sorrows that are sent to wean us from this world had reached her,
reason: Source: 'those sorrows which are sent to wean us from the earth' — candidate paraphrase adds an interpretation.

old: Haven't we lost the power to make you happy?
new: Have we lost the power to make you happy?
reason: Source: 'Have we lost the power of rendering you happy?' — negative question flips the implied answer.

old: be enough to drive away the monster lurking in my heart? Even as she spoke, I drew close to her in terror,
new: be enough to drive away the fiend lurking in my heart? Even as she spoke, I drew close to her, as if in terror,
reason: Source: 'chase away the fiend that lurked in my heart ... as if in terror' — 'fiend' changed and the hedge 'as if' dropped.

old: my fleeting, human sorrows.
new: my sorrows, which were fleeting because they were human.
reason: Source: 'my ephemeral, because human, sorrows' — the causal link is lost.

old: the valley of Chamonix.
new: the valley of Chamounix.
reason: Source prints 'Chamounix'; RULES forbid silently correcting source names to standard forms.

old: But the mighty Alps overshadowed everything, their white, shining peaks and domes towering above as if
new: But the scene was heightened and made sublime by the mighty Alps, their white, shining peaks and domes towering above everything as if
reason: Source: 'it was augmented and rendered sublime by the mighty Alps' — 'overshadowed' suggests they diminished the scene.

old: I crossed the bridge at Pelissier,
new: I crossed the bridge at Pélissier,
reason: Source: 'Pélissier' — diacritic stripped.

old: Soon I entered the valley of Chamonix
new: Soon I entered the valley of Chamounix
reason: Source prints 'Chamounix'.

old: A tingling, long-lost sense of pleasure came over me
new: A tingling, long-lost sense of pleasure often came over me
reason: Source: 'often came across me' — frequency dropped.

old: the village of Chamonix.
new: the village of Chamounix.
reason: Source prints 'Chamounix'.

old: this glorious presence-chamber of nature
new: this glorious throne room of imperial Nature
reason: Source: 'presence-chamber of imperial Nature' — 'imperial' dropped; 'presence-chamber' (a monarch's audience room) is opaque aloud.

old: Why does man boast of senses superior to animals? It only makes us more vulnerable.
new: Why does man boast of feelings more refined than those we see in animals? It only makes us more dependent creatures.
reason: Source: 'sensibilities superior to those apparent in the brute; it only renders them more necessary beings' — 'sensibilities' are feelings, not senses; 'necessary' = subject to necessity.

old: The ice field is nearly a league wide,
new: The ice field is nearly three miles wide,
reason: Candidate converts the second 'league' in this paragraph to 'three miles' but not this one; a listener hears two units.

old: so monstrously murdered!
new: so fiendishly murdered!
reason: Source: 'so diabolically murdered' — devilish register neutralized.

old: said the creature.
new: said the demon.
reason: Source: 'said the dæmon' — narrator's epithet neutralized to 'creature' (candidate renders dæmon as 'demon' elsewhere, e.g. 11,28).

old: I'm taller and stronger.
new: I'm taller than you, and my joints are more supple.
reason: Source: 'my height is superior to thine, my joints more supple' — 'stronger' replaces a specific different claim.

old: to my natural master
new: to my natural lord and king
reason: Source: 'my natural lord and king' — flattened.

old: be fair to everyone else if you must, but don't trample only on me
new: don't be fair to everyone else and trample on me alone
reason: Source: 'be not equitable to every other and trample upon me alone' — 'if you must' is added and alters the plea.

old: Misery made me a monster.
new: Misery made me a fiend.
reason: Source: 'misery made me a fiend' — the Creature's own key self-description changed.

old: Yet it's in your power to save them. Make up for what you've done. Don't reject me.
new: Yet it is in your power to make amends to me and to save them from an evil — an evil that you alone can let grow so great that not only you and your family, but thousands of others, will be swallowed up in the whirlwinds of its rage. Let your compassion be stirred, and don't reject me.
reason: Source: 'recompense me, and deliver them from an evil which it only remains for you to make so great, that ... thousands of others, shall be swallowed up in the whirlwinds of its rage' — threat dropped and 'recompense me' turned into 'make up for what you've done'.

old: judge whether I deserve your contempt or your compassion.
new: abandon me or pity me, as you judge I deserve.
reason: Source: 'abandon or commiserate me, as you shall judge that I deserve' — 'contempt' replaces 'abandon'.

old: by human law, to speak
new: by human laws, bloody as they are, to speak
reason: Source: 'by human laws, bloody as they are' — the Creature's barb dropped.

old: Just listen. If you can still condemn me after hearing my story, then destroy the work of your hands.
new: Just listen to me. Then, if you can, and if you will, destroy the work of your hands.
reason: Source: 'listen to me, and then, if you can, and if you will, destroy the work of your hands' — conditions rewritten.

old: You've left me unable to even judge whether I owe you anything.
new: You've left me no power even to consider whether I am being just to you or not.
reason: Source: 'no power to consider whether I am just to you or not' — 'owe you anything' changes the question.

old: My heart was heavy, and I didn't answer.
new: My heart was full, and I didn't answer.
reason: Source: 'My heart was full' (overflowing with feeling), not 'heavy' (which the source uses separately at the end).

old: The creature wore an expression of triumph.
new: The fiend wore an air of triumph.
reason: Source: 'the fiend with an air of exultation' — epithet neutralized to 'creature'.

old: Seating myself by the fire my detestable companion had lit, he began his tale.
new: I sat down by the fire my detestable companion had lit, and he began his tale.
reason: Dangling modifier makes it sound as if the Creature sat down; source intends Victor seated himself and the Creature began.
